_note: Entities whose Basel capital ratios are not published at the level we assess, with the last disclosure we hold and why. The score stays withheld because capital cannot be assessed at this entity, but the reason is stated plainly rather than implying we are behind on collection. Checked 7 September 2026; the virgin-money-uk entry added 3 November 2026, each statement checked against the filing it cites.

rentenbank.reason: German promotional bank, exempt from CRR since 2021; last disclosure report September 2020
rentenbank.standing: Explicitly guaranteed by the Federal Republic of Germany

nrw-bank.reason: German promotional bank, exempt from CRR since 2021; no disclosure report published since
nrw-bank.standing: Explicitly guaranteed by the State of North Rhine-Westphalia

santander-financial-services.reason: capital and leverage are measured for the Santander UK group, of which SFS is part under the Non-RFB Capital Support Deed; the company publishes no solo Basel ratios
santander-financial-services.standing: Santander UK Group Holdings plc is the head of the group for regulatory capital and leverage purposes, and members of the core UK group support each other's capital resources

goldman-sachs-international-bank.reason: the PRA sets Goldman Sachs International Bank's capital requirement individually, but the key metrics are published for Goldman Sachs Group UK Limited, its parent, and the bank issues no Pillar 3 report of its own
goldman-sachs-international-bank.standing: Goldman Sachs Group UK Limited reported a CET1 ratio of 12.7% at March 2026, and the PRA reviews the bank's own capital adequacy assessment within that group

virgin-money-uk.reason: the PRA revoked Virgin Money UK's sub-consolidation direction on 1 December 2025, ahead of the Part VII transfer of most of its subsidiary Clydesdale Bank PLC's business to Nationwide on 2 April 2026, so no Pillar 3 is published at this entity after the September 2025 interim; the company re-registered as Virgin Money UK Limited on 28 July 2026
virgin-money-uk.standing: A wholly owned subsidiary of Nationwide Building Society since 1 October 2024; its outstanding AT1 instruments stopped counting as Nationwide group own funds when the direction was revoked, but they and its externally held eligible liabilities instrument remain eligible towards the group's MREL until 31 December 2028; Clydesdale Bank PLC's own Pillar 3 is collected separately, and its report for 31 March 2026 expects none for later periods
